I'm 40 years old, farming 7 mu in Dongfu village, Anzhai township, Quzhou County. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent says at the village meetings, but I still go by what my father taught me and what the successful neighbors do. My wife works part-time at a garment factory in town, and we have two kids in school, so I need steady returns without too much risk.

This year I'm keeping all 7 mu in wheat–maize double cropping. The wheat went in last October with rotary tillage, using an improved variety. I put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and topdressed another 50 jin at green-up in March. I'll irrigate three times total — winter irrigation is already done, and I'll do two more in spring at jointing and grain-filling. For the summer maize, I'll plant hybrid seed like Nongda 372 right after wheat harvest in early June. There's barely a week between harvest and planting, so there's no time for tillage — it's no-tillage direct seeding. I'll put down compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress with urea at the big喇叭口 stage. I'll irrigate twice if it doesn't rain, and spray pesticides twice for both crops to control weeds and borers.

I thought about growing cotton like my cousin does, but it needs too much hand-picking labor and the price bounces around too much. Wheat and maize give me food security and a stable market. Last year I got about 420 kg/mu of wheat and 480 kg/mu of maize; this year I'm hoping for 450 kg/mu and 500 kg/mu if the weather holds.
